isolation_description: Fresh auditor conversation. Required source sections and scrubbed closure criteria only before implementation. No Gate C TODO, scope beyond line 86, prior audit directories or implementer summaries read. Primary source comments may identify earlier findings. Auditor identity/model/effort are dispatch labels supplied by the user, not independently measured provider telemetry. No nested agents or model APIs. Read-only discipline over the repository; the OS capability itself is not read-only. All authored artifacts, builds and caches are in the output directory.
verdict_encoding: The report-contract value fix-required encodes the single Gate C decision FAIL.

requirements.requirement: Generate review packet in HMA; bind independently observed repository root/base/head/diff/worktree, approved unit/plan/core state, unique packet/nonce/dispatch, receipt launch digests.
requirements.observation: HMA generates unique packet/nonce/dispatch and snapshots anchored root/base/target/core. Wrong-root/base/clone controls refuse. Contract-dependent packet inputs are human-deferred.

requirements.requirement: Enforce exact route, read-only review and independence from all retained unit implementations; final/disputed/high-risk family separation.
requirements.observation: Code checks read-only route and all recorded unit contributions. Final issuing reason independently triggers family separation. Existing exact-route/independence regressions pass.

requirements.requirement: Import only latest current generated dispatch once; validate exact receipt run/route/mode/completion/launch interval/packet/target/root and report hash/freshness/binding. Refuse without append.
requirements.observation: Own receipt drift/missing-field matrix, nanosecond half-open TTL controls, stale core/target/packet/snapshot tests and concurrent once-only import pass.

requirements.requirement: Validate independent-audit report contract with exact JSON/Python-compatible keys, UTF-8, types and required strings. Map only valid pass to APPROVE; final isolated; all other supported non-pass states cannot approve.
requirements.source: independent-audit report contract; v3 §4.3; v5 §3; scope §2
requirements.observation: Invalid structural reports do not approve, clear B/W, or open the host gate. Exact/UTF-8/Unicode/whitespace parity passes. Deliberate validation mutant is detected.

requirements.requirement: Snapshot findings only from exact current imported review/report/core/artifact. Failed or escalated snapshots cannot weaken prior BLOCK/WAIVABLE. Empty approving snapshot can resolve only its exact unit. Preserve legacy owner/waiver semantics, reject collisions, gate requires snapshot.
requirements.observation: Failed/escalated snapshots preserve BLOCK/WAIVABLE. Current approving own-unit snapshot resolves own findings. Exact owners, slash-source rejection, stale snapshot and legacy waiver/ownership controls pass.

requirements.requirement: Keep history compatible; distinguish legacy manual enforcement, migrate once, prohibit new manual bypass of generated review/import.
requirements.source: Gate C migration objective; task14 §4; criteria F13/A09/C-F14
requirements.observation: Baseline-written history remains readable. Mode labels distinguish legacy_manual/packet_import. Failed migrated review cannot be overridden manually. Fresh authentic imported resolution succeeds.

requirements.requirement: Bind verify-loop envelope/journal/run/unit/store/root/base; recapture argv without shell at exact target on open authorized run; retain output/hash/exit/truncation; hold core lock through capture/append; never credit criterion.
requirements.source: Gate C consolidation; v3 §3.2/§4.3; architecture §7.1; scope §4; criteria F09/A07–A08/C-F15/C-F18–C-F23/J8-03
requirements.observation: Open-run/target/envelope checks, no-shell controls, output retention/digest, no criterion credit, terminal locking pass. Executable alias bypasses operation denial: J9-01.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate audit failure → linked repair → fresh review, stale/self/failed/missing controls; preserve Gate B human stage/route/approval/evidence/terminal and concurrency guarantees.
requirements.observation: Original tests, vet, race and synthetic 17-check dogfood pass. Linked review failure/remediation/re-verification fixture passes. This does not claim Gate D/F closure.

requirements.requirement: Record every human-deferred Gate D row with unchanged exit tests and prerequisite; Gate C does not claim bounded execution, criterion credit, closure or reproduced blocker classifications.
requirements.observation: All eight deferred groups remain recorded with Gate D prerequisites and exit checks across scope §0.1, the unchanged approved proof matrix, and supplied closure criteria. The scope note alone is not a complete standalone checklist. Current code credits no criterion or launch authority. No Gate D or project-closure claim is accepted.

findings.title: Executable aliases bypass the loop recapture operation filter
findings.diagnosis: unsafeLoopArgv resolves the executable only for RejectShell, then applies destructive/network/publication checks to the original argv basenames. A stable symlink check-tool -> /usr/bin/rm bypasses the rm -r rule. Evidence.Capture admits the non-shell executable. The command deletes a scratch tree outside the repository, so before/after repository snapshots remain equal. HMA then records the successful capture in both chains. The direct identical rm command is refused. No same-UID tampering, forged ledger, route change, or Git write is needed.

evidence.observation: Resolved program identity is used at line 371 only for shell checks; operation checks at lines 380–411 classify original argv.
Capture executes admitted argv; repository-only mutation detection at line 170 cannot detect the scratch-tree deletion.

alias=false: HOST_LOOP_EVIDENCE_INVALID, sentinel remains, chains unchanged. alias=true: command_error=<nil>, sentinel absent, chain_changed=true; host result EVIDENCE_RECORDED and recapture_exit_code 0.
Independent reproduction repeats under -race in the final auditor suite.

fix.action: Apply the existing forbidden-operation checks to the resolved canonical executable identity and its argument positions before capture. Resolve symlinks and use that same approved executable path for execution. Preserve existing shell/interpreter checks and refuse resolution errors. Add direct, absolute-path and symlink-alias cases for rm, curl and git.
fix.why: The operation policy currently classifies a spelling while the OS executes its target. Checking the executed program identity closes this observed alias gap without claiming a sandbox for arbitrary compiled programs.

verification.method: Repeat TestAuditor9AliasRecursiveRemovalRefused with direct rm and check-tool -> /usr/bin/rm. Fingerprint both chains and check the sentinel before and after.
verification.expected: Both calls refuse before execution and before either append. The sentinel remains.

verification.method: Check resolved aliases to curl and git push using harmless scratch-only or admission-only controls; retain printf %s sh and normal executable controls.
verification.expected: Forbidden operations refuse through aliases; normal approved executable vectors still recapture.

verification.method: Run original go test ./..., go vet ./..., go test -race ./..., host-dogfood and independent import/terminal controls.
verification.expected: All pass after a new independently frozen review. No weakening of no-shell or terminal checks.

fix.tradeoffs: Canonical resolution must match execution on supported platforms. Deny lists do not establish safety for arbitrary compiled programs or their transitive effects. Exact approved argv binding and positive authority remain Gate D obligations.
fix.alternative: Contain immediately by refusing symlink executables in loop-evidence. This is smaller but rejects legitimate aliases. A canonical executable/argv allowlist tied to the accepted contract is stronger but depends on Gate D.

prior_findings.assessment: A newer unanswered packet invalidates an older approval and snapshot. Current packet completion is required.

closure_check.method: Run TestAuditorPendingFinalDispatchInvalidatesEarlierPass, then complete/import/snapshot the new valid final report.

prior_findings.assessment: Full contract-dependent fixed-packet inputs are human-deferred. Current core-state binding and missing accepted-plan refusal remain enforced.

prior_findings.assessment: Human acceptance of §0.1 is authoritative. Gate D obligations remain deferred, with no Gate C closure or execution-authority claim.

prior_findings.assessment: Caller-supplied Packet refuses at the CLI before append. Only review-packet creates provenance.

prior_findings.title: Loop recapture discards the verification output
prior_findings.assessment: Separate stdout/stderr remain accessible. Their framed digest and exit 7 match the evidence. Original truncation/mutation controls pass.

closure_check.method: Run TestAuditorFinalRecaptureRetainsOutput with distinct stdout and stderr, a nonzero exit and a fresh random token. Resolve OutputRef after the process ends.
closure_check.expected: Both streams remain accessible; their framed digest equals OutputDigest; exit code and truncation status match.

closure_check.method: Repeat with output above the cap and with a command that changes repository content.
closure_check.expected: Truncation is explicit and retained bytes are inspectable; mutating check still refuses evidence append.

prior_findings.title: Go reads case-variant JSON keys that the Python contract ignores
prior_findings.assessment: Go imports only the exact keys Python reads. A case variant cannot turn fix-required into pass.

closure_check.method: Import a contract-valid fix-required report with a trailing "Verdict":"pass" member against a unit with an existing BLOCK; then import its findings and check the gate.
closure_check.expected: The review is not APPROVE, the BLOCK stays, and the gate stays closed.

closure_check.method: Repeat with Unicode case-fold variants (for example U+017F long s, U+212A Kelvin sign) and case variants of keys in receipts, nested findings, hma_binding, and verify-loop state.
closure_check.expected: Go reads exactly the keys Python reads; no variant changes an import result.

prior_findings.title: Go and Python disagree on required nonempty report fields
prior_findings.assessment: U+001C–U+001F reports cannot approve. The Go/Python whitespace predicates agree over the exhaustive code-point probe.

closure_check.method: Import a receipt-bound pass report whose required strings consist only of U+001C, U+001D, U+001E, or U+001F against a unit with an existing BLOCK; then import findings and check the gate. Compare the Go whitespace predicate with Python str.isspace over all code points.
closure_check.expected: No such report approves; the BLOCK stays; the gate stays closed; the predicates agree on every code point.

prior_findings.title: Interrupted output-artifact writes are trusted as complete on retry
prior_findings.assessment: Empty, partial and symlink residue refuse before append. Complete content can be reused. Temp-write/link logic keeps final names complete.

closure_check.method: Place an empty, partial, or symlinked file at the expected artifact path, then run loop-evidence. Also run it with an intact existing artifact.
closure_check.expected: Corrupt residue is refused before either append and is preserved; an intact artifact is reused; the final name never holds incomplete bytes.

prior_findings.title: loop-evidence executes a shell command from an imported journal
prior_findings.assessment: Direct shells, shell scripts, wrappers and spelled forbidden operations refuse. A symlink to rm executes -r and appends evidence: J9-01 remains open.

closure_check.method: Run loop-evidence with journals whose verify argv is sh -c, bash <script>, env sh -c, a symlink to a shell, or an operation verify-loop forbids (git push, curl, rm -r). Call evidence.Capture directly with shell entry points.
closure_check.expected: Every case is refused before execution and before either append; plain executables still run.

prior_findings.title: Invalid UTF-8 report passes Go checks but fails the Python validator
prior_findings.assessment: Invalid UTF-8 report cannot approve. The shared decoder rejects invalid UTF-8 before typed parsing.

closure_check.method: Import a receipt-bound pass report containing an invalid UTF-8 byte against a unit with an existing BLOCK; import its findings; check the gate. Also give invalid UTF-8 to receipts and loop state.
closure_check.expected: No approval; the BLOCK stays; the gate stays closed; Go and Python agree.

prior_findings.title: The shell filter refuses a shell name used as plain data
prior_findings.assessment: printf %s sh executes as data. Direct and symlinked shell entry points refuse.

closure_check.method: Run evidence capture with printf %s sh, and with shell entry points (sh -c, a wrapper such as env or xargs given a shell, a symlinked shell).
closure_check.expected: Plain data runs; every shell entry point is refused before execution.

prior_findings.title: Executable shell scripts and wrapper aliases bypass the no-shell kernel
prior_findings.assessment: Shell and env-style shebangs and wrapper aliases refuse. The documented arbitrary-compiled-program limit remains outside this closure.

closure_check.method: Run loop-evidence and evidence.Capture with a #!/bin/sh script, a #!/usr/bin/env sh script, env plus a symlink to sh, a symlink to env plus sh and a script, and a script whose interpreter is a symlinked shell.
closure_check.expected: Each is refused before execution and before either append; plain executables and shell names as data still run. Any residual limit is recorded, not claimed closed.

prior_findings.title: A concurrent trusted core terminal append can precede loop check execution
prior_findings.assessment: The check observes the held core lock. Direct terminal append cannot pass it. Evidence precedes terminal outcome and later recapture refuses.

closure_check.method: Pause loop-evidence after its terminal check and attempt a direct core append (for example ABORTED), or probe the core run lock from inside the check.
closure_check.expected: The core lock is held from the terminal check through the core append; no check runs on a closed run.

prior_findings.title: A review with a different approved base can clear the current unit blocker
prior_findings.assessment: Wrong approved base or root refuses before a usable packet. Current root/base control remains valid.

closure_check.method: Generate review packets with base = HEAD in the approved root, with another repository root and base, and with a clone holding the approved base; then try review import and findings import against an existing BLOCK.
closure_check.expected: Each wrong base or root is refused with a named reason before a packet is usable; the BLOCK stays. Any residual root-identity limit is recorded, not claimed closed.

prior_findings.title: First generated packet can adopt another checkout and clear the current blocker
prior_findings.assessment: The root binding is explicit and written once before a packet. Unbound runs and clone-root packets refuse. Binding remains trusted-host attestation.

closure_check.method: On a run with no prior packet, generate a packet for a clone holding the approved base (with a different committed artifact), import a receipt-bound pass, then import findings against an existing BLOCK. Also try a run without any repository binding, and a second binding.
closure_check.expected: The clone packet is refused before it is usable; an unbound run cannot generate or import; the binding is written once and not taken from a packet; the BLOCK stays.

prior_findings.title: Slash-separated finding IDs collide across exact unit owners
prior_findings.assessment: Slash source IDs refuse. Duplicate global IDs also refuse before snapshot append.

closure_check.method: Import findings with id sub/F for unit U1 while unit U1/sub owns F; also attempt a snapshot that would contain a duplicate global id.
closure_check.expected: The colliding import is refused before any append; no duplicate global finding id is recorded.

prior_findings.title: Loop recapture can attach another repository artifact to an anchored unit
prior_findings.assessment: Wrong root/base or journal root refuses before command execution. Bound root/base control records evidence.

closure_check.method: Run loop-evidence naming another repository root and base, the bound root with another base, and a journal whose repo.root names another root.
closure_check.expected: Each is refused before execution and before either append; the bound root at the approved base still records evidence.

Executable-name operation admission remains a demonstrated gap, not a claim that arbitrary check binaries are sandboxed.

The operation-filter failure was reproduced only on auditor-owned scratch paths. No publication, remote request, deployment, or destructive operation on the audited repository was attempted.
Model/provider/effort identity is the user-supplied dispatch label jax / gpt-6.1-sol / high. No independent route telemetry was available in this audit session.
